disorders.name: Articulation Disorder
disorders.symptoms:
• Sound substitutions
• Sound omissions
• Sound distortions
• Low intelligibility to unfamiliar listeners
• Incorrect phonetic placement
• Structural/motor speaking strain
disorders.red_flags: No speech output by 18 months; structural anomalies (e.g., severe tongue tie); regression in sound production; high frustration/refusal to speak.

disorders.name: Phonological Disorder
disorders.symptoms:
• Predictable error patterns like fronting or stopping
• Highly unintelligible connected speech
• Final consonant deletion patterns
• Cluster reduction (dropping sound blends)
• Sound system rule confusion
disorders.red_flags: Complete lack of intelligible speech by age 3; vowel distortions; chronological mismatch (using early processes alongside advanced language).

disorders.name: Flaccid Dysarthria
disorders.symptoms:
• Marked hypernasality
• Breathy voice quality
• Visible nasal air emission
• Tongue or facial muscle atrophy/weakness
• Slurred or imprecise consonant production
disorders.red_flags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness; dynamic choking risk/aspiration on liquids; progressive fasciculations (quivering) of the tongue; weak or absent cough reflex.

disorders.name: Spastic Dysarthria
disorders.symptoms:
• Strained-strangled vocal quality
• Slow and labored speech rate
• Hyperactive gag reflex
• Monopitch and monoloudness traits
• Excessively harsh vocal emission
disorders.red_flags: Severe dysphagia (swallowing breakdown); pseudobulbar affect (uncontrollable emotional outbursts); sudden loss of airway protection during meals.

disorders.name: Ataxic Dysarthria
disorders.symptoms:
• Distinct 'drunk-sounding' speech cadence
• Irregular articulatory breakdowns
• Scanning prosody (equal/excess stress)
• Incoordinated breathing patterns
• Prolonged speech sounds/phonemes
disorders.red_flags: Sudden gait changes or falls; rapid wide-based trunk instability; explosive speech alterations or acute respiratory discoordination during phrasing.

disorders.name: Hypokinetic Dysarthria
disorders.symptoms:
• Monopitch and monoloudness
• Rapid, unprompted rushes of speech
• Micro-graphia (unusually small handwriting)
• Masked or expressionless facial features
• Progressively fading vocal intensity
disorders.red_flags: Resting tremors that suddenly worsen; profound microphonia (voice dropping to an inaudible whisper); freezing of gait or freezing of speech mid-sentence.

disorders.name: Hyperkinetic Dysarthria
disorders.symptoms:
• Involuntary vocal gasps
• Highly variable speech rate
• Sudden, involuntary voice arrests
• Dyskinesia/tremors of the jaw, tongue, or lips
• Jerky, unpredictable speech rhythm
disorders.red_flags: Sudden, involuntary respiratory gasps that disrupt airway protection; severe, unpredictable tongue protrusion or jaw spasms making chewing hazardous.

disorders.name: Mixed Dysarthria
disorders.symptoms:
• Co-occurring spastic and flaccid clinical signs
• Severely compromised speech clarity
• Inconsistent respiratory control
• Multimodal motor system weakness
• Profound intelligibility deficits
disorders.red_flags: Rapid functional decline across both cognitive and motor domains; immediate, high risk for silent aspiration; severe shortness of breath at rest.

disorders.name: Speech Sound Disorder
disorders.symptoms:
• Persistent, age-inappropriate sound errors
• Highly unintelligible to strangers
• Severe communication-related frustration
• Avoidance of verbal interactions
• Dropping early-developing phonemes
disorders.red_flags: Social isolation or school refusal due to bullying; complete mutism in front of peers; failure to acquire any new consonant sounds over a 6-month period.

disorders.name: Phonetic Disorder
disorders.symptoms:
• Isolated motoric speech sound distortions
• Persistent lateral /s/ or lisp patterns
• Incorrect tongue positioning for specific sounds
• Sound errors preserved across multiple word contexts
• Mechanical speech execution challenges
disorders.red_flags: Structural changes in the jaw/teeth causing pain; development of secondary muscular tension in the neck/throat to force sound production.

disorders.name: Speech Delay
disorders.symptoms:
• Late sound acquisition timelines
• Normal language comprehension profiles
• Noticeably low speech volume
• Simplified sound substitution habits
• Intelligibility lag compared to peers
disorders.red_flags: No word-like vocalizations by 15 months; failure to match peer group intelligibility standards by 50% or more by age 3.

disorders.name: Language Delay
disorders.symptoms:
• Late talking milestones
• Slow vocabulary growth velocity
• Normal developmental sequence but delayed speed
• Failure to use multi-word combinations by age two
• Limited communicative gestures
disorders.red_flags: Failure to respond to simple verbal requests by 18 months; complete lack of communicative intent; no warm eye-contact or joint attention.

disorders.name: Developmental Stuttering
disorders.symptoms:
• Part-word repetitions
• Prolongations of sounds
• Silent blocks / speech lockups
• Physical tension in face, jaw, or neck
• Secondary behaviors (blinking, head jerking)
disorders.red_flags: Signs of emotional situational dread; sudden escalation of silent blocks lasting >5 seconds; physical flight behaviors during speech opportunities.

disorders.name: Neurogenic Stuttering
disorders.symptoms:
• Disfluencies occur on function words
• Absence of the adaptation effect
• Sudden onset in adulthood following injury
• Disfluency across all word positions
• Minimal emotional reactivity or struggle
disorders.red_flags: Sudden concurrent onset of confusion, motor weakness, or severe headaches (indicates acute stroke or neurological episode).

disorders.name: Psychogenic Stuttering
disorders.symptoms:
• Sudden onset following emotional trauma
• Constant disfluency across all types of speaking tasks
• Regular stuttering during automatic speech tasks
• Bizarre or uncharacteristic disfluency types
• Lack of secondary struggle behaviors
disorders.red_flags: Suicidal ideation or signs of profound psychiatric crisis; active visual hallucinations or completely altered states of reality.

disorders.name: Cluttering
disorders.symptoms:
• Rapid and highly irregular speech rate
• Telescoped, compressed, or slurred words
• Poor self-awareness of speech breakdowns
• Excessive normal disfluencies (revisions/interjections)
• Disorganized sentence structures
disorders.red_flags: Complete conversational breakdown resulting in total educational/academic failure; unsafe driving or physical tasks due to rapid, disorganized processing.

disorders.name: Palilalia
disorders.symptoms:
• Involuntary repetition of one's own words
• Increasing speed during word repetitions
• Fading vocal volume towards the end of words
• Compulsive echoic behavior during dialogue
• Intact awareness but inability to stop
disorders.red_flags: Rapid escalation of comorbid motor tics or global cognitive decline; transition into total mutism due to inability to complete an initial phrase.

disorders.name: Echolalia
disorders.symptoms:
• Rote repetition of others' words or phrases
• Total lack of communicative intent
• Mirroring pitch or intonation of the speaker
• Immediate or delayed repetition styles
• Difficulty producing self-generated speech
disorders.red_flags: Complete loss of situational awareness; using echolalia exclusively to self-soothe during severe physical self-injury or panic states.

disorders.name: Aprosodia
disorders.symptoms:
• Flat, monotone voice characteristics
• Inability to express vocal emotion
• Inability to comprehend emotional inflections in others
• Lack of natural pitch variations
• Robotic or unexpressive conversational tone
disorders.red_flags: Sudden onset following unilateral right-hemisphere brain injury; severe disorientation or neglect of the left field of vision.

disorders.name: Dysprosody
disorders.symptoms:
• Distorted speech rhythm and melody
• Inappropriate stress placement on syllables
• Choppy or irregular cadence patterns
• Foreign-sounding speech qualities
• Artificial-sounding pitch swings
disorders.red_flags: Rapid changes in overall neurological functioning; sudden emergence of localized motor weakness or progressive memory loss.

disorders.name: Muscle Tension Dysphonia
disorders.symptoms:
• Severe vocal fatigue
• Sensation of throat tightness or soreness
• Strained, squeezed, or pressed vocal quality
• Frequent pitch breaks
• Loss of vocal range and projection power
disorders.red_flags: Pain radiating up to the ears during voicing; dynamic expansion of throat pain to swallowing; complete voice loss lasting over a week.

disorders.name: Spasmodic Dysphonia
disorders.symptoms:
• Intermittent strained-strangled or breathy voice breaks
• Voice breaks specifically on vowels
• Extreme physical effort required to phonate
• Normal voice during coughing, laughing, or singing
• Spasmodic movements of vocal folds on scope
disorders.red_flags: Progressive spreading of muscular tremors or spasms to the face, neck, or limbs; severe panic attacks triggered by breathing restriction.

disorders.name: Vocal Nodules
disorders.symptoms:
• Bilateral vocal fold callouses
• Chronic hoarseness
• Loss of high vocal pitch range
• Breathy, raspy vocal quality
• Vocal exhaustion during short conversations
disorders.red_flags: Hemoptysis (coughing up blood or blood-tinged mucus); acute breathing stridor; complete absence of phonation (aphonia) for more than 2 weeks.

disorders.name: Vocal Polyps
disorders.symptoms:
• Unilateral fluid-filled lesion
• Diplophonia (hearing two distinct pitches at once)
• Sudden, acute hoarseness onset
• Sensation of a lump in the throat (globus)
• Breathy and strained vocal emission
disorders.red_flags: Sudden, acute respiratory distress if a large pedunculated polyp falls into the airway; rapid expansion of airway closure during exertion.

disorders.name: Vocal Cysts
disorders.symptoms:
• Unilateral internal mass on vocal fold
• Asymmetric mucosal wave vibration
• Persistent hoarseness
• Severe breathiness
• Chronic vocal exhaustion
disorders.red_flags: Total loss of vocal mucosal wave; chronic localized throat pain that interferes with adequate nutritional intake.

disorders.name: Reinke Edema
disorders.symptoms:
• Abnormally low pitch
• Deep, gravelly, or 'smoky' voice quality
• Heavy fluid swelling along the vocal folds
• Chronic history of heavy smoking
• Shortness of breath during exertion
disorders.red_flags: Inspiratory stridor at rest; waking up gasping for air (obstructive sleep apnea symptoms caused by massive vocal fold swelling).

disorders.name: Vocal Fold Paralysis
disorders.symptoms:
• Severe, permanent breathiness
• Weak, ineffective cough reflex
• Total aphonia (loss of voice) or near-whisper
• Frequent choking or coughing on liquids
• Inability to protect the airway during a swallow
disorders.red_flags: Recurrent aspiration pneumonia; chronic, silent coughing bouts during drinking; cyanosis (turning blue) during attempts to swallow liquids.

disorders.name: Vocal Fold Paresis
disorders.symptoms:
• Rapid vocal fatigue with use
• Unstable pitch control
• Weakness when projecting or shouting
• Intermittent breathy intervals
• Increased respiratory effort while speaking
disorders.red_flags: Sudden development of fluid management issues (coughing/spluttering during meals); progressive shortness of breath when executing normal dialogue.

disorders.name: Chronic Laryngitis
disorders.symptoms:
• Hoarseness lasting over 3 weeks
• Globus sensation (lump in throat)
• Persistent dry, hacking cough
• Raw, burning sensation in the larynx
• Intermittent complete loss of voice
disorders.red_flags: Unexplained weight loss paired with chronic hoarseness in an adult; palpable hard lumps or lymph nodes in the neck structure.

disorders.name: Functional Aphonia
disorders.symptoms:
• Whispered speech production
• Completely normal cough and throat clear reflexes
• Sudden onset tied to psychological factors
• Complete absence of laryngeal structural pathology
• Variable voicing patterns outside conscious speech
disorders.red_flags: Inability to execute an emergency throat clear or cough; profound social isolation; underlying severe major depressive or trauma behaviors.

disorders.name: Presbyphonia
disorders.symptoms:
• Thin, weak, or frail voice
• Age-related bowing of the vocal folds
• Elevated male pitch range
• Reduced volume and vocal projection
• Short, breathy phrase delivery
disorders.red_flags: Frequent choking fits in an elderly individual; profound weight loss due to fear of swallowing; progressive social withdrawal.

disorders.name: Voice Tremor
disorders.symptoms:
• Rhythmic pitch oscillations
• Rhythmic loudness oscillations on sustained vowels
• Shaky, unsteady vocal character
• Tremor worsens under stress or fatigue
• Involuntary laryngeal muscle quivering
disorders.red_flags: Difficulty safely swallowing pills or thin liquids due to coordinated laryngeal structural tremors; sudden loss of general balance/gait.

disorders.name: Puberphonia
disorders.symptoms:
• Inappropriately high pitch past puberty in biological males
• Breathy, weak voice quality
• Frequent, embarrassing pitch breaks
• Inability to access lower register/chest resonance
• Strained speech delivery
disorders.red_flags: Severe depressive symptoms; absolute refusal to speak in school or public settings; signs of high psychological distress or self-harm.

disorders.name: Ventricular Dysphonia
disorders.symptoms:
• Deep, severely strained voice quality
• False (ventricular) vocal fold vibration
• Rough, harsh vocal output
• High muscle strain during speech initiation
• Rapid vocal exhaustion and throat aching
disorders.red_flags: Severe tissue hypertrophy or underlying hidden laryngeal tumors forcing false vocal fold closure; severe breathing constraints.

disorders.name: Contact Ulcer / Granuloma
disorders.symptoms:
• Sharp throat pain radiating to the ear
• Chronic morning throat clearing
• Persistent hoarseness
• Constant tickling sensation in the throat
• Pain aggravated by speaking loudly
disorders.red_flags: Spitting up blood; excruciating pain that limits the ability to swallow solid foods; progressive airway restriction from large granuloma mass.

disorders.name: Sulcus Vocalis
disorders.symptoms:
• Indented groove along the vocal fold edge
• Breathy and hoarse voice quality
• High effort needed to talk
• Notable loss of volume
• Restrictive, stiff mucosal wave action
disorders.red_flags: Rapid development of secondary hyper-functional laryngeal muscle patterns causing severe, chronic neck muscle tension and head pain.

disorders.name: Vocal Fold Scar
disorders.symptoms:
• Stiff, unyielding vocal fold tissue
• Severely restricted dynamic pitch range
• High vocal effort and strain
• Harsh, rough, and dry voice quality
• Incomplete vocal fold closure (air leakage)
disorders.red_flags: Total permanent loss of functional communication; severe daily laryngeal fatigue leading to total professional or academic breakdown.

disorders.name: Laryngeal Papillomatosis
disorders.symptoms:
• Progressive, severe hoarseness
• Inspiratory stridor (noisy breathing)
• Shortness of breath / respiratory distress
• Warty, cauliflower-like growths in airway
• Chronic throat irritation and weak cry
disorders.red_flags: Acute cyanosis; visible retractions of the chest or ribs when trying to breathe; sudden total occlusion of the larynx airway.

disorders.name: Laryngopharyngeal Reflux
disorders.symptoms:
• Frequent post-nasal drip sensations
• Morning hoarseness
• Chronic throat clearing habits
• Globus sensation (lump in throat)
• Chronic cough and sour taste in mouth
disorders.red_flags: Laryngospasm episodes (sudden waking up gasping for air with a locked airway); chronic bleeding in throat; severe burning chest pain.

disorders.name: Conversion Voice Disorder
disorders.symptoms:
• Total aphonia (complete loss of voice)
• Sudden onset matching psychological triggers
• Completely normal larynx structure and movement
• Retained non-speech voicing (cough/laugh)
• Anxiety or stress-linked presentation
disorders.red_flags: Emergence of comorbid conversion symptoms like sudden functional blindness or paralysis of a limb; severe acute psychiatric trauma.

disorders.name: Paradoxical Vocal Fold Motion
disorders.symptoms:
• Acute airway obstruction
• Inspiratory stridor (gasping sound)
• Sudden panic and anxiety symptoms
• Chest or throat tightness during breathing
• Symptoms mimic asthma but fail to respond to inhalers
disorders.red_flags: Total loss of consciousness due to lack of oxygen; severe blue coloration of lips/face; panic leading to extreme physiological shock.

disorders.name: Chronic Cough Voice
disorders.symptoms:
• Non-productive cough lasting over 8 weeks
• Hyper-sensitive larynx
• Throat tickle triggered by temperature or talking
• Vocal hoarseness following coughing episodes
• Sensation of airway irritation
disorders.red_flags: Coughing causing rib fractures, syncope (fainting), or vomiting; presence of bloody sputum; severe localized chest wall pain.

disorders.name: Hypernasality
disorders.symptoms:
• Excessive nasal resonance on oral vowels
• Muffled speech clarity
• Weak oral pressure consonants (p, b, t)
• Snorting noises during connected speech
• Nasal grimacing or flaring during talk
disorders.red_flags: Nasopharyngeal regurgitation of foods/liquids; chronic, severe malnutrition in infants; immediate loss of speech intelligibility under 20%.

disorders.name: Hyponasality
disorders.symptoms:
• Total lack of nasal resonance on m, n, ng
• Speech sounds like having a severe cold
• Persistent mouth breathing habits
• Chronic nasal congestion feelings
• Muffled, blocked speech sounds
disorders.red_flags: Severe obstructive sleep apnea with gasping; failure to thrive due to feeding/breathing coordination breakdown in young children.

disorders.name: Cul-de-sac Resonance
disorders.symptoms:
• Hollow, 'trapped' sound profile
• 'Potato-in-the-mouth' voice quality
• Sound trapped in oral/nasal cavity with no exit
• Significant loss of conversational volume
• Structural blockage signs (e.g., enlarged tonsils)
disorders.red_flags: Acute airway obstruction; massive swelling of palatine or pharyngeal tonsils causing sleep apnea or dynamic swallowing blockages.

disorders.name: Velopharyngeal Insufficiency
disorders.symptoms:
• Structural gap in the soft tissue palate
• Audible nasal air emission
• Glottal stop substitutions (throat popping)
• Inability to whistle or blow air out of the mouth
• Hypernasal vowel distortions
disorders.red_flags: Frequent choking or aspiration of solid foods through the nasal pathway; profound failure to gain weight or develop structural speech.

disorders.name: Velopharyngeal Incompetence
disorders.symptoms:
• Intact structure but poor neurological movement
• Severe, fluctuating hypernasality
• Nasal regurgitation of liquids during meals
• Inconsistent palatal elevation
• Weak intraoral pressure during speech
disorders.red_flags: Sudden global onset of other neurological deficits (e.g., cranial nerve palsies); high silent aspiration risks across multiple food groups.

disorders.name: Adenoid Hypertrophy
disorders.symptoms:
• Chronic mouth breathing
• Persistent hyponasality
• Loud, disruptive snoring / sleep apnea
• Stuffy nasal speech markers
• Persistent nasal discharge and open-mouth posture
disorders.red_flags: Development of 'adenoid facies' structural skull deformations; chronic fluid accumulation in middle ear leading to permanent conductive hearing loss.

disorders.name: Nasal Emission Disorder
disorders.symptoms:
• Audible air escape from the nose on pressure sounds
• Weak pressure on sounds like /p/, /t/, /s/
• Facial grimacing near the nostrils during speech
• Choppy, short phrasing pattern
• Friction noise coming from the nasal passage
disorders.red_flags: Development of permanent compensatory pharyngeal or laryngeal maladaptive speech sound productions that make later surgical outcomes poor.

disorders.name: Cleft Lip Speech Disorder
disorders.symptoms:
• Labial sound distortions on /p/, /b/, /m/
• Visible lip restriction or tight scar tissue
• Poor bilabial seal formation
• Compensatory dental or tongue speech placements
• Distorted facial aesthetics during expression
disorders.red_flags: Dehiscence (splitting open) of a post-surgical lip repair; severe feeding failure due to inability to create an adequate forward seal on breast/bottle.

disorders.name: Cleft Palate Speech Disorder
disorders.symptoms:
• Pervasive hypernasality
• Compensatory pharyngeal fricative/glottal substitutions
• Continuous nasal air emissions during talking
• Delayed speech sound acquisition milestones
• Severe feeding/sucking challenges in infancy
disorders.red_flags: Profound failure to thrive; recurrent severe middle ear infections leading to high fever and permanent tympanic membrane damage.

disorders.name: Submucous Cleft Palate
disorders.symptoms:
• Hypernasal speech distortions
• Bifid (split) uvula feature
• Bluish midline zone along the soft palate
• Hidden notch in the hard palate bone
• Frequent history of middle ear infections
disorders.red_flags: Sudden, severe onset of hypernasality following a routine adenoidectomy procedure (revealing the previously hidden submucous palate defect).

disorders.name: Velocardiofacial Syndrome
disorders.symptoms:
• Severe hypernasality and VPI
• Significant verbal language delay
• Distinct facial structural traits
• Learning or cognitive challenges
• Adaptive speech difficulties
disorders.red_flags: Acute cardiac anomalies or fainting spells (linked to underlying conotruncal heart defects common in this genetic syndrome).

disorders.name: Developmental Language Disorder
disorders.symptoms:
• Persistent language deficits
• Short, simple sentence structures
• Poor grammar and syntax errors
• Word-finding difficulties in conversation
• Trouble following complex story plots
disorders.red_flags: Severe physical aggression due to inability to communicate needs; complete academic failure by early grade levels.

disorders.name: Expressive Language Disorder
disorders.symptoms:
• Intact language comprehension
• Frequent word-finding pauses
• Simplified verbal sentence output
• Grammatical errors in tense use
• Difficulty describing events or telling stories
disorders.red_flags: Extreme withdrawal and refusal to speak in public; development of intense selective mutism traits or severe emotional anxiety.

disorders.name: Receptive Language Disorder
disorders.symptoms:
• Failure to follow verbal directions
• Echoing questions instead of answering
• Poor recall of abstract spoken items
• Inappropriate responses to peer conversations
• Looking to others for behavioral cues
disorders.red_flags: Inability to understand basic danger warnings (e.g., 'stop', 'hot'); high risk for physical injury due to comprehension gaps.

disorders.name: Mixed Receptive-Expressive
disorders.symptoms:
• Global language deficits in understanding and talking
• Apparent social withdrawal
• Consistently low academic performance scores
• Highly restricted vocabulary size
• Short, telegraphic phrases
disorders.red_flags: Total communication breakdown; inability to report basic personal pain, sickness, or immediate safety needs to caregivers.

disorders.name: Pragmatic Language Disorder
disorders.symptoms:
• Inappropriate social remarks
• Poor conversational turn-taking
• Rigidly literal mind (misses humor/sarcasm)
• Inability to maintain a topic of conversation
• Inadequate eye contact and poor body language rules
disorders.red_flags: Severe vulnerability to exploitation or bullying; total peer ostracization and lack of functional relationship building.

disorders.name: Semantic Language Disorder
disorders.symptoms:
• Overuse of vague words like 'thing' or 'stuff'
• Trouble understanding synonyms or idioms
• Limited depth of vocabulary knowledge
• Word-retrieval blocks during descriptions
• Highly literal semantic interpretations
disorders.red_flags: Severe academic regression; absolute inability to comprehend core textbook context or curriculum concepts by age 8.

disorders.name: Specific Language Impairment
disorders.symptoms:
• Frequently dropping grammatical morphemes (e.g., '-ed')
• Completely normal non-verbal IQ profile
• Short mean length of utterance (MLU)
• History of being a late talker
• Persistent errors in syntax rules
disorders.red_flags: Significant social alienation; reading and literacy development arrest resulting in persistent functional illiteracy.

disorders.name: Late Language Emergence
disorders.symptoms:
• Less than 50 spoken words by 24 months old
• Complete lack of 2-word combinations
• Limited or absent use of communicative gestures
• Heavy reliance on pointing or crying for needs
• Delays in early vocal milestones
disorders.red_flags: No communicative progress or loss of any words/gestures between 12 and 24 months old (strong indicator of autism/neurodegenerative regression).

disorders.name: Autism Spectrum Disorder
disorders.symptoms:
• Poor or fleeting eye contact
• Complete lack of response to name being called
• Restricted, repetitive interests or play styles
• Echolalia or scripting from television/movies
• Difficulties navigating shared social interactions
disorders.red_flags: Severe self-injurious behaviors (head-banging, biting); profound sensory meltdowns causing physical danger; total lack of danger awareness.

disorders.name: Social Communication Disorder
disorders.symptoms:
• Pervasive pragmatic language failures
• Normal structural grammar and vocabulary
• Inability to adjust communication style to context
• Trouble reading non-verbal social cues
• Ineffective conversational repair strategies
disorders.red_flags: Extreme vulnerability to social grooming, exploitation, or online scams due to complete inability to process subtext or bad intent.

disorders.name: Selective Mutism
disorders.symptoms:
• Total silence in specific social locations (e.g., school)
• Speaks completely normally or excessively at home
• High social anxiety or frozen posture when approached
• Uses gestures, nodding, or whispering in public
• Avoidance behavior lasting longer than a month
disorders.red_flags: Inability to report illness, physical abuse, or emergency situations at school; complete academic non-participation and functional immobility.

disorders.name: Intellectual Disability
disorders.symptoms:
• Global communication delays across all domains
• Language skills match a low cognitive age
• Concrete comprehension limits (cannot grasp abstract ideas)
• Simplified, immature sentence structure
• Slow processing and learning rates
disorders.red_flags: Loss of basic self-care and adaptive skills; wandering or elopement behaviors combined with an inability to state personal identification details.

disorders.name: Down Syndrome
disorders.symptoms:
• Articulation errors due to an enlarged tongue
• Receptive skills are significantly stronger than expressive
• Breathier or husky vocal quality
• Delayed grammar acquisition timelines
• Short, simplified phrase patterns
disorders.red_flags: Sudden regression in motor skills or neck pain (indicative of dangerous atlantoaxial instability); signs of early-onset Alzheimer's disease.

disorders.name: Fragile X Syndrome
disorders.symptoms:
• Jittery, fast, or cluttered speech pacing
• Conversational phrase perseveration (repeating ideas)
• Active gaze avoidance (looking away)
• Tangential, off-topic discourse habits
• Social anxiety indicators
disorders.red_flags: Severe, unmanageable aggressive physical outbursts; rapid development of seizures or major cardiac mitral valve prolapse issues.

disorders.name: Rett Syndrome
disorders.symptoms:
• Severe regression of hand and speech milestones
• Periods of hyperventilation or breath holding
• Stereotypic hand-wringing or clapping
• Complete loss of purposeful spoken words
• Severe physical motor coordination decline
disorders.red_flags: Sudden, life-threatening cardiac arrhythmias; prolonged, severe central apnea episodes (breath-holding that leads to cyanosis).

disorders.name: Williams Syndrome
disorders.symptoms:
• 'Cocktail party' talkative personality
• Extremely shallow vocabulary depth
• High generalized anxiety traits
• Highly descriptive but structurally hollow narratives
• Exceptional rote auditory memory but weak math/spatial logic
disorders.red_flags: Sudden chest pain or severe hypertension episodes (linked to hypercalcemia or supravalvular aortic stenosis common to the disorder).

disorders.name: Childhood Disintegrative Disorder
disorders.symptoms:
• Profound regression in speech and social skills after 2+ years of normal growth
• Loss of bowel/bladder control
• Emergence of severe repetitive behaviors
• Loss of motor skills and play habits
• Total breakdown of functional language
disorders.red_flags: Rapid, continuous loss of foundational functions over days/weeks; emergence of status epilepticus (continuous seizure activity).

disorders.name: Fetal Alcohol Spectrum
disorders.symptoms:
• Persistent memory gaps and learning blocks
• Poor narrative cohesion (scrambled stories)
• Executive functioning and planning problems
• Difficulty understanding social boundary parameters
• Attention deficits and impulsivity
disorders.red_flags: High risk for legal system involvement due to total lack of impulse control; absolute inability to recognize physical exploitation or unsafe peer structures.

disorders.name: Angelman Syndrome
disorders.symptoms:
• Complete absence of verbal speech
• Frequent unprovoked laughter and happy demeanor
• Severe cognitive delay markers
• Hand-flapping movements and jerky gait
• Total reliance on non-verbal cues/AAC systems
disorders.red_flags: Severe, drug-resistant epilepsy (status epilepticus); profound sleep architecture fragmentation causing severe caregiver exhaustion/safety risks.

disorders.name: Prader-Willi Syndrome
disorders.symptoms:
• Unclear speech sound distortions
• Hypernasal vocal resonance
• Slowed articulatory movements
• Restricted expressive vocabulary boundaries
• Delayed narrative generation skill sets
disorders.red_flags: Life-threatening hyperphagia (insatiable eating) leading to acute gastric rupture; morbid obesity-related sudden respiratory failure or choking.

disorders.name: Childhood Apraxia of Speech
disorders.symptoms:
• Inconsistent errors on consonants and vowels
• Distinct vowel distortions
• Visible articulatory groping behaviors
• Prosody and rhythm issues
• Increased breakdown on longer words
disorders.red_flags: Loss of previously spoken words; limited or absent canonical babbling in infancy; severe feeding issues; completely unable to imitate sounds on command.

disorders.name: Acquired Apraxia of Speech
disorders.symptoms:
• Articulatory groping during speech attempts
• Severely slowed rate of speech
• Automatic speech is better than volitional speech
• Distorted sound substitutions
• Awareness of errors leading to frustration
disorders.red_flags: Sudden, catastrophic loss of speech coordination post-stroke/trauma; dynamic deterioration of speech control; high anxiety and complete communication withdrawal.

disorders.name: Dyspraxia of Speech
disorders.symptoms:
• Difficulty segmenting syllables
• Sequencing errors in multi-syllabic targets
• Trial-and-error oral groping
• Lost speech control under pressure
• Inconsistent performance on repetition tasks
disorders.red_flags: Complete verbal blockages lasting several seconds; observable tremor of the lips during speech attempts; dynamic frustration leading to aggressive outbursts.

disorders.name: Verbal Apraxia
disorders.symptoms:
• Loss of volitional, purposeful speech control
• Pervasive sound substitutions
• Severe physical struggle behaviors during speech
• Speech initiation delays
